extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, organisations, and stakeholders who want to find, take part in, or submit responses to Scottish Government consultations
extracted.subtask_description: A government consultations portal listing open and closed consultations, showing closing dates, providing draft/summary/Easy Read materials, and describing how responses are published and taken into account in final decisions or strategies. The page signals procedural expectations for consultees (e.g., reviewing materials, submitting before closing) and explains outputs (published responses, summaries, government responses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inform your response by the draft and supporting documents
rubrics_metrics.description: "Your response to this consultation should be informed by the refreshed draft Supporting Children's Learning Code of Practice and we recommend that you review this before responding. A summary and an Easy Read are also available."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultees are explicitly advised to review the consultation draft and accompanying summary and Easy Read materials before submitting a response. Where such documents are provided, they form the basis for an informed response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit responses by the consultation closing date
rubrics_metrics.description: Each consultation entry shows a closing date (e.g. "Closes 11 May 2026").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses must be submitted before the stated closing date for the consultation; consultees should check the 'Open Consultations' list for current deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible supporting materials should be provided and used
rubrics_metrics.description: The page indicates that consultations may provide a summary and an Easy Read (accessible) version of documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultations may include accessible formats (summaries, Easy Read) and consultees are encouraged to consult those formats when responding; organisers are expected to publish such accessible materials when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of responses, summaries and government response
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultation outputs include published responses and analysis and a government response (e.g. "A full set of responses to this consultation can be viewed through the 'Published responses' link"; "A summary of consultation answers and the government response has been published").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultation organisers will normally publish received responses, a summary of feedback, and a government response explaining how feedback was considered; consultees can expect transparency about how responses were handled and the opportunity to view published responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responses will be analysed and can lead to changes in policy or strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples show that consultation feedback is analysed and has informed updates (e.g. Draft Circular Economy Strategy: 'An independent analysis was carried out... Headline updates to the strategy include...' ; ESS strategy: 'All of the responses were considered and have helped to inform the preparation of a final version of the Proposed Strategy').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultation responses may be subject to independent analysis and the findings can lead to concrete changes in strategy, updated wording, additional policy mechanisms, or preparation of final proposals to be submitted to Parliament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responses are categorised by respondent type and campaign responses are reported
rubrics_metrics.description: The page reports respondent breakdowns (e.g. 'We received 26 responses... 2 responded as individuals and 24 on behalf of an organisation.' and 'we also received over 1200 campaign responses from Friends of the Earth Scotland').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organisers count and categorise responses (individuals, organisations, campaign responses) and report these totals in consultation outcomes; consultees should be aware that mass/campaign responses are recorded and reported alongside individual/organisational replies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation process may include statutory/legislative steps after consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: Environmental Standards Scotland strategy: 'All of the responses were considered and have helped to inform the preparation of a final version of the Proposed Strategy that was submitted to the Scottish Parliament for approval. The Scottish Parliament now has 40 days to consider the Strategy... If approved the Strategy will then be published...'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some consultations feed into formal processes (e.g., submission to Parliament) and are therefore constrained by statutory steps and timelines; consultees should understand that outcomes may proceed through formal approval processes after consultation.
